To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

in Scapharca dimeric hemoglobin the photodissociation process is not accompanied by a large structural rearrangement, as in the tetramer, and the photoproduct is not in equilibrium with the deoxy species at 300 K.
the photodissociation of dimeric Sc. hemoglobin leads to a photoproduct that is stable on the 10- ns time scale, but relaxes to the deoxy derivative within 1 micros.

the near-infrared charge-transfer band of dimeric Sc. hemoglobin is sensitive to the heme-heme interaction in the photodissociation process and in the deoxy state, and that the band III peak position is sensitive to the temperature of the deoxy state.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the photoproduct of the hemoglobin dimer of the bivalve Scapharca inaequivalvis.
the characterization of the deoxygenated and the photodissociation products in the near-infrared region, and it is the first study of the photodissimilated derivative of a dimeric hemoglobin.
the near-infrared spectra of the hemoglobin of the bivalve mollusk Scapharca inaequivalvis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
band III is a good probe of the heme-heme interaction in dimeric hemoglobins, since it is very sensitive to structural changes of the hemes and to their relative positions.
in the deoxy dimer the heme-heme interactions are stronger and the heme-hemoprotein interaction is weaker than in the photodissociate.
, in the photoproduct, the iron is in the ferrous state and the heme is not fully planar, but is still slightly ruffled.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the photodissociation of the heme iron from the oxygen in dimeric hemoglobin is not a simple one-step process but is accompanied by a series of conformational changes in the hemoglobin structure.
in the dimeric Scaparca hemoglobin, in contrast to the tetrameric hemoglobin from the same animal, the relaxation process is very slow.
the photoproduct of the hemoglobin dimer is characterized by a charge transfer band shifted toward longer wavelengths with a peak position that is independent of temperature.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in the dimeric Scrapharca hemoglobin, the near-infrared charge-transfer band is a sensitive probe of the heme-heme distance, as well as of the heme-ligand distance, and that it can be used to monitor relaxation processes in this protein.
the photoproduct of the carbonmonoxygenated derivative is a good mimic of the deoxy derivative, at least in the first 10-ns time range.

the relaxation of the photodissociation product to the deoxy state occurs in two steps: first, a rapid (10 ns) relaxation of the heme iron to the deoxy position, and then, a slower (microsecond time scale) relaxation of the protein to the deoxy conformation.
